subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive and other request-scoped contexts, or should background-only behavior remain the contract?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but fixing it changes the meaning of an existing shipped trust key and model-override authorization boundary.

options.title: Widen The Existing Grant
options.body: Land or revise the linked fix so explicit plugin-scoped trust applies to interactive plugin subagent runs, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal flags.

options.title: Keep Background-Only
options.body: Reject the behavior change and update SDK docs plus runtime errors so operators know the key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

options.title: Narrow Scoped Trust First
options.body: Combine the fix with a stricter request-scope boundary, such as excluding external plugin HTTP route contexts before merge.

recommendation.title: Widen The Existing Grant
recommendation.body: Land or revise the linked fix so explicit plugin-scoped trust applies to interactive plugin subagent runs, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal flags.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the trusted plugin subagent override policy and is the strongest history owner for the config-contract decision.
